children: Cardano developers now have a public environment for preparing the Dijkstra upgrade, but its name needs careful reading. The test network is available; the transition to Dijkstra’s new protocol rules is still a separate step.
A live rehearsal environment comes before new rules

The sequence is set out in Intersect’s weekly report and the Cardano Operations Book. Pool operators can obtain configuration files, connect to the test network and use a faucet for test assets. The planned Dijkstra transition follows availability of the 11.2 prerelease and a hard-fork initiation action.

For developers, that staging creates a useful baseline. A wallet or indexer can establish that it handles the present environment correctly before it is asked to interpret changed transaction formats and protocol behavior. If everything changes at once, distinguishing an application bug from a network-upgrade problem becomes much harder.

The published node release provides the actual software reference. A version number in a roadmap should never substitute for checking which release a network configuration requires. Public test assets also have no relationship to the value of mainnet ADA.
NewsBTC has covered the same operational distinction during Ethereum’s Hoodi postponement: being ready for an earlier configuration does not guarantee readiness for the next one.
Readiness is broader than upgrading a pool

Stake pools are one part of the exercise. Exchanges need deposits and withdrawals to remain intelligible, wallets need accurate balances and signatures, and applications need their transactions to be accepted under the intended rules. A testnet gives those teams a shared place to expose mismatches before real assets depend on the answers.

It also changes what observers should measure. The number of announcements about an upgrade says little about whether independent teams have completed their checks. Useful evidence includes compatible releases, successful synchronization, working transaction submission and identified problems that have been fixed.

That is relevant to the adoption questions behind Cardano’s stablecoin activity. An application ecosystem needs reliable infrastructure as well as liquidity. Likewise, the concerns in NewsBTC’s Solana resilience coverage show why network performance is only one part of a usable platform.

The public Dijkstra environment is a tangible preparation milestone. It does not announce a mainnet activation date, establish that every proposed feature is already running, or guarantee a particular ADA price response. Its immediate value is more practical: the next round of compatibility work can happen on a network that other participants can inspect and join.
Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
Intersect’s October 24 update says the refreshed Dijkstra testnet became public on October 21.
It currently runs Conway protocol version 11 with node 11.1.3.
A later node prerelease and testnet governance action are needed for protocol version 12.

title: Cardano Opens Dijkstra Testnet While The Upgrade Itself Awaits Its Next Step
